name: Int_Reciprocal_Sqrt_2
questiontext: Complete the square in the quadratic expression q which is given by \[ q= {{CT:0}}, \] and use this to evaluate the following integral \[ \int {{CT:1}}d{{CT:2}} \] [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback:
Completing the square for q gives \[q={{CT:3}}{{CT:4}} + {{CT:5}}{{CT:2}} + {{CT:6}}={{CT:3}}{{CT:4}}+ {{CT:7}}{{CT:2}}+{{CT:8}}+{{CT:9}}=({{CT:10}}{{CT:2}}+{{CT:11}})^2 + {{CT:9}}\]

Therefore \[\int{{CT:1}}d{{CT:2}} = \int\frac{1}{{CT:12}}d{{CT:2}}=\int\frac{1}{{CT:13}}d{{CT:2}}\]

 

Let \({{CT:14}}+{{CT:15}} = \sinh(u)\)

giving \[d{{CT:2}} = {{CT:16}}du\]

Therefore \[\int{{CT:1}}d{{CT:2}} = \int\frac{1}{{CT:17}}{{CT:18}}du\]

and since \(\cosh^2(u)-\sinh^2(u) = 1\)

\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle \int\frac{1}{{CT:19}}{{CT:20}}du&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle\int\frac{1}{{CT:21}}{{CT:20}}du\\  \int \frac{du}{{CT:10}}&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \frac{u}{{CT:10}} + c \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:22}} \end{array}\]
